question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: Right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of magnetic field around a straight conductor.
option_2: Right-hand thumb rule cannot be applied to circular loops.
option_3: Right-hand thumb rule can be used to find the force on a conductor in a magnetic field.
option_4: Right-hand thumb rule cannot be applied to a straight conductor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of magnetic field around a straight conductor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The right-hand thumb rule (Maxwell's rule) states: if a current-carrying straight conductor is held in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of current flow, the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field around it. (दायें हाथ का अंगूठा नियम — धारावाही चालक के चारों ओर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा)

 

• This rule applies equally well to a straight conductor and to a circular loop — for a loop, curling the fingers in the direction of current makes the thumb point along the axis in the direction of the field.

 

• To find the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field, a different rule is used — Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, not the right-hand thumb rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is used for motors: it gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (thumb = force/motion, forefinger = field, middle finger = current).

 

• Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is used for generators: it gives the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.

 

• The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire are concentric circles centred on the wire, lying in a plane perpendicular to it.

 

NOTE

 

• Right-hand thumb rule cannot be applied to circular loops (Option B): Incorrect — the rule applies to loops too; the thumb then shows the direction of the field at the centre of the loop.

 

• Right-hand thumb rule can be used to find force (Option C): Incorrect — force direction is found using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, not the thumb rule.

 

• Right-hand thumb rule cannot be applied to a straight conductor (Option D): Incorrect — this is precisely the standard case for which the rule was devised.

question: Through which part of the female reproductive system does the egg travel from the ovary to the uterus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fallopian tube.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fallopian tube (oviduct) is the narrow tube that carries the egg (ovum) released from the ovary towards the uterus, and it is also the usual site of fertilisation. (डिंबवाहिनी नली — अंडाणु का मार्ग)

 

• Each ovary has one Fallopian tube leading to the uterus; the funnel-shaped end near the ovary has finger-like projections called fimbriae that sweep the released egg into the tube.

 

• If the egg is fertilised by a sperm in the Fallopian tube, the resulting zygote travels down the tube and implants in the uterus wall, where the embryo develops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The uterus (womb) is a pear-shaped, muscular organ where the foetus develops during pregnancy.

 

• The cervix is the narrow lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

 

• The vagina is the muscular canal connecting the cervix to the exterior of the body; it receives sperm and also serves as the birth canal.

 

NOTE

 

• Cervix (Option A): The narrow neck connecting the uterus to the vagina, not the passage for the egg from the ovary.

 

• Vagina (Option B): The outer canal of the reproductive tract; sperm enter through it but the egg does not travel through it towards the uterus.

 

• Ureter (Option D): Part of the excretory system, carrying urine from the kidney to the bladder — unrelated to the reproductive system.

question: A convex lens has a focal length of 25 cm. What is the power of this convex lens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is +4.0 D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The power of a lens is given by P = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres. (लेंस की क्षमता — P = 1/f)

 

• Given f = 25 cm = 0.25 m, so P = 1/0.25 = +4.0 D (dioptre).

 

• A convex (converging) lens always has a positive power, since its focal length is taken as positive by sign convention; a concave (diverging) lens has negative power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B, i.e. +4.0 D. (Note: the options as printed in the source show a formatting glitch where the leading digit '4' has been replaced by the option's own letter, e.g. 'A).0 D' instead of '4.0 D' — reproduced here exactly as it appears in the original paper.)

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of power of a lens is the dioptre (D), and 1 D = 1 m⁻¹.

 

• A lens of shorter focal length has greater power (more converging/diverging ability); power is inversely proportional to focal length.

 

• Optometrists prescribe spectacle lenses in dioptres — a convex lens (+ power) corrects hypermetropia, and a concave lens (− power) corrects myopia.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, C and D: All represent the same magnitude (4.0 D) with different signs/labels due to the printing glitch in the source; only Option B carries the '+' sign correctly associated with a converging (convex) lens as intended by the key.

question: A farmer wants to improve both the quantity and quality of honey produced on their farm. What practice should they adopt?
option_1: Keep the bees in shaded areas away from plants
option_2: Ensure nectar-rich flowers bloom throughout the season
option_3: Reduce the number of flowering plants
option_4: Remove all wildflowers from the area
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ensure nectar-rich flowers bloom throughout the season.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Honey bees make honey from the nectar of flowers, so a continuous and abundant supply of nectar-rich flowers throughout the season directly improves both the quantity and quality of honey produced. (पुष्प रस — शहद उत्पादन का आधार)

 

• This is the basic principle behind apiculture (bee-keeping) — bee boxes/colonies are placed near fields of mustard, sunflower, litchi, or other nectar-rich crops so that bees have continuous forage.

 

• Keeping bees away from flowers, removing flowering plants, or removing wildflowers all reduce the nectar available to bees and would lower honey production, not improve it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Apiculture is the science of rearing honey bees for honey and wax; India is a major producer, especially in states like Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Bees also perform pollination, which increases the yield of many crops — this makes bee-keeping beneficial to overall agriculture, not just honey output.

 

• Common Indian honey bee species include Apis cerana indica, Apis dorsata (rock bee), and the introduced Apis mellifera (Italian/European bee), used widely in commercial apiculture.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep bees in shaded areas away from plants (Option A): Cuts off bees from nectar sources and would reduce honey production.

 

• Reduce the number of flowering plants (Option C): Directly reduces nectar availability, harming both quantity and quality of honey.

 

• Remove all wildflowers (Option D): Wildflowers are an important nectar source for bees, especially outside the main crop-flowering season; removing them hurts honey production.

question: What is the role of the pollen tube in plant fertilisation?
option_1: To transport the male germ cell to the female germ cell
option_2: To transport pollen grains to the stigma
option_3: To produce the male germ cell
solution_text:
The correct answer is To transport the male germ cell to the female germ cell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After pollination, the pollen grain lands on the stigma and germinates, growing a thin tube called the pollen tube, which travels down the style to the ovary. (पराग नलिका — नर जनन कोशिका का परिवहन)

 

• The pollen tube's essential function is to carry the male gamete (male germ cell) through the style into the ovule, where it fuses with the female gamete (egg cell) during fertilisation to form the zygote.

 

• Pollination (transfer of pollen to the stigma) happens before the pollen tube forms — it is a separate, earlier step carried out by agents like wind, water, insects, or birds, not by the pollen tube itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fertilisation in flowering plants is often called double fertilisation, since one male gamete fuses with the egg to form the zygote, and another fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm.

 

• After fertilisation, the ovule develops into a seed, and the ovary develops into a fruit.

 

• The male gametes are produced inside the pollen grain (in the anther), while the female gamete (egg cell) is produced inside the embryo sac within the ovule.

 

NOTE

 

• To transport pollen grains to the stigma (Option B): This describes pollination, which occurs before pollen tube formation, not the role of the pollen tube itself.

 

• To produce the male germ cell (Option C): The male germ cells are produced within the pollen grain, not by the pollen tube; the tube only carries them.

 

• To form the zygote (Option D): The zygote is formed by the fusion of male and female gametes after the pollen tube delivers the male gamete — the tube itself does not form the zygote.

question: Which of the following cells has dendrite on one end?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neuron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, and it has branch-like extensions called dendrites at one end that receive signals from other neurons. (न्यूरॉन — डेंड्राइट, तंत्रिका कोशिका)

 

• The neuron has three main parts: the cell body (cyton), dendrites (which receive nerve impulses), and a long axon (which carries the impulse away from the cell body to the next neuron or an effector organ).

 

• Nerve impulses travel from dendrite → cell body → axon → synapse → dendrite of the next neuron, allowing rapid transmission of information across the body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The junction between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next is called a synapse, where chemical messengers called neurotransmitters are released.

 

• Neurons are classified as sensory (carry impulses from receptors to the brain/spinal cord), motor (carry impulses from the CNS to muscles/glands), and relay/interneurons (connect sensory and motor neurons).

 

• Unlike most body cells, mature neurons generally do not divide, and the longest human cell — the neuron running from the spinal cord to the toe — can be over a metre long.

 

NOTE

 

• Red blood cell (Option B): A biconcave, enucleate cell that carries oxygen via haemoglobin; it has no dendrites.

 

• Monocyte (Option C): A type of white blood cell (leukocyte) involved in immunity; it is not a nerve cell and has no dendrites.

 

• Platelet (Option D): A small, disc-shaped cell fragment involved in blood clotting; it has no dendrites.

question: Work done by a constant force is zero if:
option_3: displacement is zero or perpendicular to force
solution_text:
The correct answer is displacement is zero or perpendicular to force.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done by a force is defined as W = F × s × cosθ, where F is the force, s is the displacement, and θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. (कार्य — W = F.s.cosθ)

 

• Work is zero in two situations: when the displacement is zero (s = 0, even if force is applied, e.g. pushing a wall that doesn't move), or when the force acts perpendicular to the displacement (θ = 90°, so cos90° = 0, e.g. a coolie carrying a load horizontally while gravity acts vertically downward).

 

• The magnitude of the force being large or variable does not by itself make work zero — what matters is the angle between force and displacement, and whether displacement occurs at all.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Work is positive when θ is between 0° and 90° (force has a component in the direction of motion), and negative when θ is between 90° and 180° (e.g. friction opposing motion).

 

• The SI unit of work is the joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N × 1 m.

 

• A classic example of zero work: in uniform circular motion, the centripetal force is always perpendicular to the velocity (displacement direction), so it does no work on the object.

 

NOTE

 

• Force is variable (Option A): A varying force does not by itself make work zero; work still depends on the force-displacement relationship at each instant.

 

• Force is large (Option B): A large force generally does more work, not zero, unless displacement is zero or perpendicular.

 

• Displacement is small (Option D): Small displacement gives small (not necessarily zero) work; only zero displacement or perpendicular force-displacement gives exactly zero work.

question: Which among the following is NOT a physical characteristic of ionic compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Insoluble in water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water (a polar solvent) because water molecules surround and separate the oppositely charged ions, so 'insoluble in water' is NOT a characteristic of ionic compounds. (आयनिक यौगिक — जल में घुलनशील)

 

• Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points because a large amount of energy is needed to break the strong electrostatic forces of attraction holding the ions together in the crystal lattice.

 

• They conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution, because the ions become free to move and carry charge; however, in the solid state, ions are fixed in the lattice and cannot move, so solid ionic compounds do not conduct electricity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ionic compounds are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal (which loses electrons to form a cation) to a non-metal (which gains electrons to form an anion), e.g. NaCl, where Na loses one electron to Cl.

 

• Ionic compounds are typically hard and brittle — the crystal shatters when force is applied because like-charged ions are forced to align, causing repulsion.

 

• In contrast, covalent compounds generally have low melting/boiling points, are often insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents, and do not conduct electricity (except a few exceptions).

 

NOTE

 

• High melting point (Option A) and High boiling point (Option B): Both are genuine characteristics of ionic compounds due to strong lattice forces.

 

• Conducts electricity in molten state (Option D): A true characteristic — molten (or dissolved) ionic compounds conduct electricity because their ions are free to move.

question: Which of the chemical formulae represents bleaching powder?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ca(ClO)₂.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bleaching powder, also called calcium oxychloride or chloride of lime, has the chemical formula CaOCl₂, commonly represented as Ca(ClO)₂ / Ca(OCl)₂ — calcium hypochlorite. (विरंजक चूर्ण — Ca(OCl)Cl / Ca(ClO)₂)

 

• It is prepared industrially by passing chlorine gas through dry slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂]: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

 

• Bleaching powder is widely used as a bleaching agent for cotton and linen in the textile industry, for bleaching wood pulp in paper factories, and as a disinfectant for drinking water and swimming pools because it releases chlorine, which kills microorganisms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bleaching powder gives a strong smell of chlorine and reacts with dilute acids to release chlorine gas, which is the basis of its bleaching/disinfecting action.

 

• It is also used in the manufacture of chloroform and as an oxidising agent in various chemical processes.

 

• Slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂, used to make bleaching powder, is itself made by adding water to quick lime (CaO), which is obtained by heating limestone (CaCO₃).

 

NOTE

 

• Ca2(ClO)2 (Option A): Not a correctly balanced or standard formula for bleaching powder.

 

• Ca(ClO2)2 (Option C): This would represent calcium chlorite, a different chlorine oxo-compound, not bleaching powder.

 

• Ca(ClO2) (Option D): An incorrectly balanced/invalid formula (calcium is divalent and would need two ClO₂⁻ ions), not bleaching powder.

question: Which of the following options is INCORRECT regarding when rate of evaporation increases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increase in humidity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Evaporation is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point, from the surface of the liquid. (वाष्पीकरण — तापमान, सतह क्षेत्रफल, हवा की गति से बढ़ता है)

 

• The rate of evaporation increases with an increase in surface area (more molecules exposed at the surface), an increase in temperature (molecules gain more kinetic energy and escape faster), and an increase in wind speed (removes water vapour molecules from near the surface, keeping the surrounding air less saturated).

 

• The rate of evaporation decreases with an increase in humidity, because humid air already contains more water vapour and can hold less additional vapour, slowing further evaporation — so 'increase in humidity' increasing evaporation is the incorrect statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Evaporation causes cooling — this is why sweating cools the human body, and why water kept in an earthen pot (matka) stays cool (evaporation from the porous surface absorbs latent heat from the remaining water).

 

• Boiling differs from evaporation in that it occurs throughout the liquid (not just the surface) and only at the liquid's fixed boiling point.

 

• The latent heat of vaporisation is the heat energy absorbed by a substance at its boiling point to convert from liquid to vapour without a change in temperature.

 

NOTE

 

• Increase in surface area (Option A): A true factor that increases evaporation rate — a spread-out liquid evaporates faster than the same volume in a narrow container.

 

• Increase in temperature (Option B): A true factor — higher temperature gives molecules more kinetic energy to escape as vapour.

 

• Increase in wind speed (Option C): A true factor — wind carries away vapour molecules, maintaining a vapour concentration gradient that speeds up evaporation.

question: Which of the following movements is brought about by voluntary muscles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Movement of tongue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Voluntary muscles (skeletal muscles) are under conscious control of the brain and can be moved at will, such as the muscles of the tongue, arms, legs, and face. (ऐच्छिक पेशियाँ — मस्तिष्क के सचेत नियंत्रण में)

 

• The tongue is made of skeletal muscle and its movements (talking, chewing, swallowing initiation) are voluntary — we consciously decide to move it.

 

• Movements of the heart, stomach walls, and intestines are all involuntary — they are controlled automatically by the autonomic nervous system and hormones, and cannot be consciously started or stopped.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muscles are classified into three types: striated (skeletal, voluntary), smooth (visceral, involuntary), and cardiac (involuntary but striated).

 

• Cardiac muscle is unique — it is striated in appearance like skeletal muscle, but functions involuntarily and continuously throughout life without fatigue.

 

• Smooth muscle lines the walls of internal organs like the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels, and produces slow, rhythmic, involuntary contractions such as peristalsis (wave-like movement that pushes food through the digestive tract).

 

NOTE

 

• Movement of heart (Option B): Cardiac muscle contraction is involuntary and self-regulated by the sino-atrial node (natural pacemaker).

 

• Movement in the stomach walls (Option C): Caused by smooth muscle, involuntary, part of digestion (churning of food).

 

• Movement in intestines (Option D): Also caused by smooth muscle via involuntary peristalsis, moving food/waste along the digestive tract.

question: What are the two main properties of carbon that contribute to its 'versatile nature' and its ability to form a large number of compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Catenation and tetravalency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Catenation is the unique ability of carbon atoms to form strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, creating long chains, branched chains, and rings — no other element shows this property to such an extent. (श्रृंखलन एवं चतुःसंयोजकता — कार्बन की बहुसंख्यक यौगिक बनाने की क्षमता)

 

• Tetravalency means carbon has 4 valence electrons and can form 4 covalent bonds with other carbon atoms or with atoms of other elements (H, O, N, S, halogens, etc.), giving rise to an enormous diversity of stable compounds.

 

• Together, these two properties explain why carbon forms millions of organic compounds — far more than all other elements combined — ranging from simple methane (CH₄) to complex biomolecules like proteins and DNA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Because carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bonds are strong and covalent, most carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points, are generally poor conductors of electricity, and are often combustible.

 

• Allotropy (existence in different physical forms like diamond, graphite, fullerene) and isomerism (same molecular formula, different structure) are also features associated with carbon chemistry, but they are consequences of, not the primary cause of, its versatile bonding nature.

 

• Diamond (hardest natural substance, each C bonded to 4 others in a rigid 3D network) and graphite (soft, layered, good conductor) are the two well-known crystalline allotropes of carbon.

 

NOTE

 

• Good conductivity and sonorous nature (Option B): These are typical properties of metals, not of carbon (except graphite, a partial exception, which conducts electricity but isn't sonorous).

 

• High melting point and ductility (Option C): Ductility is a metallic property; most carbon (organic) compounds actually have low melting points, not high.

 

• Isomerism and allotropy (Option D): These are interesting features related to carbon chemistry but are not the fundamental reason for its bond-forming versatility — catenation and tetravalency are the root causes.

question: Which of the following is true regarding loudness of sound?
option_4: Loudness depends on the speed of wave.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loudness depends on the amplitude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loudness of sound is a measure of the energy carried by the sound wave, and it depends on the amplitude of the wave — larger amplitude means louder sound. (प्रबलता — आयाम पर निर्भर करती है)

 

• Loudness is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude; it is measured in decibels (dB).

 

• Pitch (how shrill or grave a sound is), on the other hand, depends on the frequency of the sound wave — higher frequency gives a higher pitch. Wavelength and speed are related to frequency but do not, by themselves, determine loudness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The quality (timbre) of a sound, which lets us distinguish between two sounds of the same loudness and pitch (e.g. a violin and a flute playing the same note), depends on the waveform of the sound.

 

• The audible range for the human ear is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; sounds below 20 Hz are infrasonic and above 20,000 Hz are ultrasonic.

 

• The speed of sound in a medium depends on the elasticity and density of that medium, and is generally: solids > liquids > gases.

 

NOTE

 

• Loudness depends on the wavelength (Option A): Incorrect — wavelength relates to pitch (via frequency), not loudness.

 

• Loudness depends on the frequency (Option B): Incorrect — frequency determines pitch, not loudness.

 

• Loudness depends on the speed of wave (Option D): Incorrect — the speed of a sound wave is fixed by the medium it travels through, not by loudness.

question: Which of the following shows acidic behaviour in aqueous solution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is HCl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• HCl (hydrochloric acid) is an acid — when dissolved in water, it ionises to release H⁺ (hydrogen) ions, HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻, which is the defining characteristic of acidic behaviour in aqueous solution. (अम्लीय व्यवहार — H⁺ आयन उत्पन्न करना)

 

• Substances that release H⁺ ions in water are acids (turn blue litmus red, taste sour); substances that release OH⁻ ions in water are bases (turn red litmus blue, taste bitter, feel soapy).

 

• Ca(OH)₂ (calcium hydroxide/slaked lime), NaOH (sodium hydroxide/caustic soda), and KOH (potassium hydroxide/caustic potash) are all bases, since they release OH⁻ ions in solution, not H⁺.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acids react with active metals to release hydrogen gas: e.g. Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂↑, tested with a burning matchstick (pop sound).

 

• Acids react with metal carbonates/bicarbonates to release carbon dioxide gas: e.g. Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑.

 

• The pH scale (0 to 14) measures acidity/basicity: values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral (pure water), and above 7 are basic/alkaline.

 

NOTE

 

• Ca(OH)2 (Option A): A base (slaked lime), used in whitewashing and to make bleaching powder.

 

• NaOH (Option B): A strong base (caustic soda), used in soap-making and paper industry.

 

• KOH (Option D): A strong base (caustic potash), used in making liquid soaps.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about average speed?
option_1: To find speed, we need both the magnitude and direction of the object
option_2: Average speed only needs the magnitude, not direction
option_3: Its SI unit is metres per second (m/s)
option_4: Speed is calculated as distance divided by time
solution_text:
The correct answer is To find speed, we need both the magnitude and direction of the object.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Speed is a scalar quantity — it is fully described by its magnitude alone, and does not require direction. This makes 'to find speed we need both magnitude and direction' the incorrect/NOT true statement asked for in the question. (चाल — अदिश राशि, केवल परिमाण)

 

• Speed = distance travelled ÷ time taken; since distance is a scalar, speed is also a scalar.

 

• The SI unit of speed is metres per second (m/s), and average speed for the whole journey is total distance divided by total time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, velocity is a vector quantity — it needs both magnitude and direction, since velocity = displacement ÷ time, and displacement is a vector.

 

• Acceleration, defined as the rate of change of velocity, is also a vector quantity.

 

• Uniform speed means equal distances are covered in equal intervals of time, while non-uniform speed means unequal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

 

NOTE

 

• Average speed only needs magnitude, not direction (Option B): This is a true statement about speed (a scalar quantity) — hence not the answer, since the question asks for the NOT-true option.

 

• Its SI unit is m/s (Option C): True — the SI unit of speed (and velocity) is metres per second.

 

• Speed is calculated as distance divided by time (Option D): True — this is the standard formula for (average) speed.

question: Which of the following best explains the term 'formula unit mass'?
option_1: The mass of a single atom of an element
option_2: The total mass of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound
option_3: The mass of a single molecule of an element
option_4: The mass of one mole of a substance
solution_text:
The correct answer is The total mass of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Formula unit mass is defined as the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms present in one formula unit of an ionic compound (as given by its chemical formula). (सूत्र इकाई द्रव्यमान — यौगिक के एक सूत्र में सभी परमाणुओं का कुल द्रव्यमान)

 

• The term 'formula unit mass' is used specifically for ionic compounds (like NaCl), which do not exist as discrete molecules but as a repeating lattice of ions; the term 'molecular mass' is reserved for covalent/molecular substances.

 

• Example: formula unit mass of NaCl = atomic mass of Na (23 u) + atomic mass of Cl (35.5 u) = 58.5 u.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atomic mass is the mass of a single atom of an element expressed in atomic mass units (u), relative to 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

 

• Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule of a substance (used for covalent compounds like H₂O, CO₂).

 

• Molar mass is the mass of one mole (6.022 × 10²³ particles) of a substance, numerically equal to the atomic/molecular/formula unit mass but expressed in grams per mole (g/mol).

 

NOTE

 

• The mass of a single atom of an element (Option A): This defines atomic mass, not formula unit mass.

 

• The mass of a single molecule of an element (Option C): This describes molecular mass, applicable to molecular substances, not the ionic 'formula unit' concept.

 

• The mass of one mole of a substance (Option D): This describes molar mass, a related but distinct concept measured in grams, not atomic mass units.

question: If a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field and the direction of current is reversed, the force on the conductor ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is reverses direction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, and its direction depends on both the direction of the current and the direction of the magnetic field. (धारा की दिशा उलटने पर बल की दिशा भी उलट जाती है)

 

• When the direction of the current is reversed while the magnetic field stays the same, the direction of the force also reverses (though its magnitude stays the same, since F = BIL sinθ depends on the magnitudes of B, I, L, and θ, none of which change).

 

• This principle — force reversing with current direction — is the basis of how a DC motor's split-ring commutator works: it periodically reverses the current in the coil so that the resulting force keeps the coil rotating in the same direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The magnitude of the force is given by F = BIL sinθ, where B is the magnetic field strength, I is the current, L is the length of the conductor in the field, and θ is the angle between the current and field directions.

 

• The force is maximum when the conductor is placed perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°) and zero when it is parallel to the field (θ = 0°).

 

• This force is the working principle behind electric motors, which convert electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

 

NOTE

 

• Remains the same (Option A): Incorrect — reversing current direction reverses the direction of the resulting force (by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule).

 

• Becomes zero (Option B): Incorrect — reversing current does not make the force zero; the force only becomes zero if the conductor is parallel to the field, or if the current itself becomes zero.

 

• Doubles (Option D): Incorrect — merely reversing the direction of current does not change the magnitude of the force, only its direction.

question: Which type of meristematic tissue is responsible for increase in the height of plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apical meristem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Apical meristem is located at the growing tips of roots and shoots and is responsible for primary growth, i.e. increase in the length/height of the plant. (शीर्षस्थ विभज्योतक — पौधे की लम्बाई में वृद्धि)

 

• Apical meristem cells are constantly dividing, adding new cells that elongate the stem and root, and it is also responsible for the formation of leaves and flower buds.

 

• In contrast, lateral meristem (also called cambium) is present along the sides of stems and roots and is responsible for secondary growth, i.e. increase in girth/thickness, not height.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Based on location, meristems are classified as apical (tips), intercalary (base of leaves/internodes, e.g. in grasses, responsible for regrowth after grazing/mowing), and lateral (sides).

 

• Cambium (vascular cambium and cork cambium) is a type of lateral meristem responsible for the formation of secondary xylem and phloem, increasing stem/root diameter over years — this is how tree trunks widen, seen as annual growth rings.

 

• Meristematic cells are characterised by thin cell walls, dense cytoplasm, prominent nuclei, and no vacuoles, and they retain the ability to divide throughout the plant's life (unlike most permanent tissue).

 

NOTE

 

• Lateral meristem (Option B): Responsible for increase in girth/width, not height.

 

• Cambium (Option C): A specific type of lateral meristem; also responsible for secondary (width-wise) growth, not height.

 

• Secondary meristem (Option D): Develops later in the plant's life (e.g. from mature tissue that becomes meristematic again, like cork cambium) and is generally associated with secondary/lateral growth, not increase in height.

question: Select the group of organisms in which asexual reproduction occurs by fission.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blue-green algae.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria), being unicellular prokaryotic organisms, reproduce asexually mainly by binary fission — the parent cell simply divides into two identical daughter cells. (नील हरित शैवाल — विखंडन द्वारा जनन)

 

• Fission is a common mode of asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms such as bacteria, amoeba, and blue-green algae, where the organism splits into two (binary fission) or many (multiple fission) new individuals.

 

• Seed plants and flowering plants (all higher, multicellular plants) do not reproduce by fission — they mainly reproduce sexually via seeds/flowers, or asexually via vegetative propagation (cuttings, runners, tubers, etc.), spores, or budding, but not fission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common asexual reproduction methods in plants: vegetative propagation (e.g. potato tubers, sugarcane cuttings), spore formation (e.g. ferns, mosses), and budding (e.g. yeast, though yeast is a fungus not a plant).

 

• Binary fission examples: Amoeba, Paramecium, and most bacteria.

 

• Multiple fission (splitting into many daughter cells at once) is seen in organisms like Plasmodium (the malaria parasite) under favourable conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• All seed plants (Option A) and Flowering plants (Option B): Both reproduce mainly through seeds (sexual reproduction) or vegetative propagation, not fission.

 

• All plants (Option C): Too broad and incorrect — the plant kingdom as a whole does not reproduce by fission; this is characteristic of simple unicellular organisms like cyanobacteria.

question: The defect in which a person cannot see distant objects clearly but can see nearby objects is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is myopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Myopia (near-sightedness/short-sightedness) is the defect in which a person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects clearly, because the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina instead of on it. (निकट दृष्टि दोष — दूर की वस्तु स्पष्ट नहीं दिखती)

 

• Myopia occurs due to excessive curvature of the eye lens or elongation of the eyeball, causing light rays from distant objects to converge before reaching the retina.

 

• It is corrected using a concave lens (diverging lens) of suitable power, which diverges the incoming light rays slightly before they enter the eye, so that they now focus exactly on the retina.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is the opposite defect — a person can see distant objects clearly but not nearby ones, corrected using a convex lens.

 

• Presbyopia is an age-related defect where the eye's power of accommodation gradually decreases due to weakening of the ciliary muscles, often corrected using bifocal lenses.

 

• Astigmatism occurs when the cornea or lens is not perfectly spherical, causing blurred vision at all distances, and is corrected using a cylindrical lens.

 

NOTE

 

• Hypermetropia (Option B): The opposite of myopia — the person cannot see nearby objects clearly (far-sightedness).

 

• Astigmatism (Option C): Caused by an irregularly curved cornea, leading to blurred vision at any distance, not specifically distant objects.

 

• Presbyopia (Option D): An age-related loss of near-vision accommodation, unrelated to the specific inability to see distant objects.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about the 'Attraction of particles of matter'?
option_1: The force of attraction is different for different particles.
option_2: The force of attraction is less in liquids as compared to gases.
option_3: The force of attraction is same for different particles.
option_4: The force of attraction is more in liquids as compared to solids.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The force of attraction is different for different particles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The intermolecular force of attraction between particles of matter is not the same for all substances — it varies depending on the nature of the substance, which is why different materials exist in different physical states (solid, liquid, gas) under the same conditions. (कणों के मध्य आकर्षण बल — पदार्थ के अनुसार भिन्न-भिन्न)

 

• In solids, the force of attraction between particles is the strongest, giving solids a definite shape and volume; in liquids, it is intermediate; and in gases, it is the weakest, allowing gas particles to move freely and occupy all available space.

 

• Since the strength of this attraction differs from one substance to another (and across states), the general statement that it is 'different for different particles' correctly captures this variability.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three states of matter are distinguished mainly by two factors: intermolecular force of attraction and intermolecular space (or kinetic energy of particles).

 

• Order of force of attraction: solids > liquids > gases; order of intermolecular space: gases > liquids > solids.

 

• Changes of state (melting, boiling, freezing, condensation) occur when the balance between attraction and thermal/kinetic energy of particles is altered by adding or removing heat.

 

NOTE

 

• Force of attraction is less in liquids compared to gases (Option B): Incorrect — it is actually the reverse; liquids have a stronger attractive force between particles than gases.

 

• Force of attraction is same for different particles (Option C): Incorrect — this force varies significantly between different substances and states of matter.

 

• Force of attraction is more in liquids compared to solids (Option D): Incorrect — solids have the strongest force of attraction among the three states, not liquids.

question: The most common electrolyte to be used for electrolytic refining of copper would be the solution of acidified:
solution_text:
The correct answer is copper sulphate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the electrolytic refining of copper, an acidified copper sulphate (CuSO₄) solution is used as the electrolyte. (तांबे के विद्युत अपघटनी शोधन में — अम्लीकृत कॉपर सल्फेट विलयन)

 

• In this process: the impure copper is made the anode, a strip of pure copper is made the cathode, and the electrolyte is acidified CuSO₄ solution. On passing current, pure copper dissolves from the anode and gets deposited on the cathode, while insoluble impurities (gold, silver, etc.) settle down as anode mud.

 

• The acid (dilute H₂SO₄) is added to increase the conductivity of the solution and prevent hydrolysis of the copper sulphate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• This process is an application of electrolysis and follows Faraday's laws of electrolysis.

 

• The valuable metals recovered from the anode mud (like gold and silver) are often a significant economic by-product of copper refining.

 

• Similar electrolytic refining is used for other metals too — e.g. nickel is refined using acidified nickel sulphate solution.

 

NOTE

 

• Copper oxide (Option A): Not soluble enough to serve as an effective electrolyte for this process.

 

• Copper carbonate (Option B): Insoluble in water, so it cannot function as an electrolyte solution.

 

• Copper chloride (Option C): Not the standard electrolyte used industrially for copper refining; acidified copper sulphate is the conventional choice.

question: Which of the following situations involves an unbalanced force?
option_1: A car moving with uniform speed on a straight road
option_2: A ball rolling on the ground and eventually stopping
option_3: A book kept on a table
option_4: A person standing still on the ground
solution_text:
The correct answer is A ball rolling on the ground and eventually stopping.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An unbalanced force is a net non-zero force that causes a change in the state of motion of an object — i.e. it accelerates, decelerates, or changes the direction of the object. (असंतुलित बल — वस्तु की गति की अवस्था में परिवर्तन)

 

• A rolling ball gradually slowing down and stopping is decelerating due to the unbalanced force of friction acting opposite to its motion — since its speed is changing (decreasing to zero), the net force acting on it cannot be zero.

 

• In the other three cases (car moving at uniform speed, book resting on a table, person standing still), the object's state of motion is not changing — meaning the forces acting on each are balanced (net force = 0), even though multiple forces (like gravity and normal reaction) may be acting simultaneously.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• This question tests Newton's First Law of Motion (law of inertia): an object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced (net) external force.

 

• Balanced forces do not change the speed or direction of an object — e.g. a book on a table has gravity pulling it down balanced exactly by the table's normal reaction force pushing up.

 

• Friction is a very common source of unbalanced force in everyday situations, decelerating moving objects like rolling balls, sliding boxes, or coasting vehicles.

 

NOTE

 

• A car moving with uniform speed (Option A): Uniform speed means no change in the state of motion, so the net force is balanced (zero).

 

• A book kept on a table (Option C): The book is at rest and stays at rest — gravity and the table's normal force are balanced.

 

• A person standing still on the ground (Option D): The person remains at rest, so the forces of gravity and the ground's normal reaction are balanced.

question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true about the pressure exerted by fluids?

 

I. Fluids exert pressure on the base and walls of the container in which they are enclosed.

 

II. Pressure exerted in any confined mass of fluid is transmitted unequally in different directions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only (i).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Fluids (liquids and gases) exert pressure in all directions on the walls and base of the container that encloses them, due to the weight of the fluid and the random motion/collision of its particles against the container surface. (द्रव दाब — तल एवं दीवारों पर दाब)

 

• Statement II is incorrect: According to Pascal's Law, pressure exerted anywhere in a confined mass of fluid is transmitted equally in all directions — not unequally as stated. Statement II reverses this well-known law, making it false.

 

• Since only Statement I is factually correct, the answer is Only (i).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pascal's Law is the basis of many hydraulic devices such as the hydraulic press, hydraulic jack, hydraulic brakes, and lifts, which use a small force applied over a small area to create a large force over a large area.

 

• Fluid pressure at a point depends on the depth below the surface, the density of the fluid, and the acceleration due to gravity: P = hρg.

 

• Pressure exerted by a fluid acts perpendicular to the surface it touches, at every point of contact.

 

NOTE

 

• Only (ii) (Option A): Incorrect — Statement II is factually wrong (pressure is transmitted equally, not unequally, per Pascal's Law).

 

• Neither (i) nor (ii) (Option C): Incorrect — Statement I is factually correct, so this cannot be the answer.

 

• Both (i) and (ii) (Option D): Incorrect — since Statement II incorrectly reverses Pascal's Law, both statements cannot be true together.

question: Which incident was responsible for the beginning of the Chipko Movement in the village of Reni?
option_2: Approval given to a contractor to fell trees near the village
option_3: Sale of forest by local residents
option_4: Government decision to use forest land for farming
solution_text:
The correct answer is Approval given to a contractor to fell trees near the village.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chipko Movement began in Reni village (Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, then part of Uttar Pradesh) in 1974, when the government gave a contractor permission to fell a large number of trees near the village, threatening the local forest ecology and villagers' livelihood. (चिपको आंदोलन — रैणी गाँव, पेड़ों की कटाई की अनुमति)

 

• When the men of the village were away and the contractor's workers arrived to cut the trees, local women led by Gaura Devi rushed to the forest and hugged (chipko) the trees, physically preventing them from being cut, forcing the loggers to retreat.

 

• This method of resistance — embracing trees to stop them from being felled — gave the movement its name, 'Chipko' (meaning 'to stick/hug' in Hindi), and it later spread across the Himalayan region, becoming a landmark event in India's environmental history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chipko Movement is often traced back to an earlier 1973 incident in Mandal village, also in Chamoli, led by activists like Chandi Prasad Bhatt and the Dashauli Gram Swarajya Sangh (DGSS), but the Reni incident (1974) with Gaura Devi is the most iconic episode.

 

• Sunderlal Bahuguna, another key figure, gave the movement its ecological slogan 'Ecology is permanent economy' and later led the associated fight against the Tehri Dam.

 

• The movement's success led to a 15-year ban on green felling in the Himalayan forests of Uttar Pradesh by the government (announced by Indira Gandhi in 1980), and it became an inspiration for environmental movements worldwide.

 

NOTE

 

• Industrial development planned by villagers (Option A): Incorrect — the villagers opposed, rather than planned, the destructive activity; the movement was a protest against tree felling.

 

• Sale of forest by local residents (Option C): Incorrect — it was the government/contractor's action to fell trees, not a sale by local residents.

 

• Government decision to use forest land for farming (Option D): Incorrect — the specific trigger was permission for commercial tree-felling by a contractor, not conversion of forest land to farmland.

question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 7, 11 and 13?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 6006.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find which option is divisible by 7, 11 and 13 simultaneously.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since 7, 11 and 13 are pairwise co-prime (no common factors), a number divisible by all three must be divisible by their product: 7 × 11 × 13 = 1001.

 

• Check each option for divisibility by 1001: 6006 ÷ 1001 = 6 exactly (1001 × 6 = 6006). ✓

 

• The other options (2121, 1546, 3026) do not divide evenly by 1001.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember 7 × 11 × 13 = 1001. Any multiple of 1001 (1001, 2002, 3003, 4004, 5005, 6006, ...) is automatically divisible by 7, 11 and 13. Just scan the options for a multiple of 1001.

 

NOTE

 

• This 1001 trick is very handy for RRB-level number-system questions asking about simultaneous divisibility by 7, 11 and 13.

question: What is the length of the altitude (in cm) to the side QR of a triangle PQR with side PQ = 25 cm, PR = 25 cm and QR = 40 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle PQR: PQ = PR = 25 cm (isosceles), QR = 40 cm (base).

 

SOLUTION

 

• In an isosceles triangle, the altitude from the apex (P) to the base (QR) bisects the base.

 

• Half of QR = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm.

 

• By Pythagoras theorem in the right triangle formed: altitude² = PQ² − (QR/2)² = 25² − 20² = 625 − 400 = 225.

 

• Altitude = √225 = 15 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise the Pythagorean triplet: 15, 20, 25 = 5 × (3, 4, 5). Since PQ = 25 (hypotenuse-like side) and half-base = 20, the altitude is instantly the third member of the triplet = 15.

 

NOTE

 

• The altitude from the apex of an isosceles triangle always bisects the base and is perpendicular to it — this creates two congruent right triangles, letting you apply Pythagoras directly.

question:
If a gymnastic coach has 14 gymnasts, their heights are as follows (in cm):

172, 173, 164, 178, 168, 169, 173, 172, 173, 164, 178, 168, 169, 173

 

The mode of this data (in cm) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 173.

 

GIVEN

 

• Heights (cm): 172, 173, 164, 178, 168, 169, 173, 172, 173, 164, 178, 168, 169, 173 (14 values).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Count the frequency of each value: 172 → 2 times; 173 → 4 times; 164 → 2 times; 178 → 2 times; 168 → 2 times; 169 → 2 times.

 

• The mode is the value that occurs most frequently. Here, 173 occurs 4 times, more than any other value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Tally each distinct value quickly in one pass; the value with the visibly repeated highest count (173 appears at positions 2, 7, 9 and 14) is the mode — no need to sort the whole list.

 

NOTE

 

• Mode = most frequently occurring value in a data set; a data set can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), or more.

question: The sum of the present ages of Ankita and her daughter Anushree is 50 years. Five years ago from now, Ankita was three times as old as Anushree. What is the present age (in years) of Anushree?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Present age of Ankita + present age of Anushree = 50.

 

• 5 years ago, Ankita's age = 3 × Anushree's age (5 years ago).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Ankita's present age = A, Anushree's present age = S. So A + S = 50 ... (i)

 

• 5 years ago: (A − 5) = 3(S − 5) ⇒ A − 5 = 3S − 15 ⇒ A = 3S − 10 ... (ii)

 

• Substitute (ii) into (i): (3S − 10) + S = 50 ⇒ 4S = 60 ⇒ S = 15.

 

• (Check: A = 50 − 15 = 35. 5 years ago: Ankita = 30, Anushree = 10; 30 = 3 × 10 ✓)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up two linear equations directly from 'sum of ages' and 'ratio condition x years ago/hence', then solve by substitution — this is the standard method for all such age-ratio problems.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify your answer by plugging both ages back into both conditions of the question — it catches sign errors quickly.

question: Sheethal spends 60% of her monthly salary on household expenses. If the remaining amount after her spending is ₹33,200, what is her monthly salary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹83,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Household expenses = 60% of salary; remaining amount = ₹33,200.

 

SOLUTION

 

• If 60% is spent, remaining = 100% − 60% = 40% of salary.

 

• 40% of salary = ₹33,200 ⇒ Salary = 33,200 ÷ 0.40 = ₹83,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remaining % = 40% = 2/5 of salary. So Salary = Remaining amount × (5/2) = 33,200 × 2.5 = ₹83,000.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert 'remaining after x% spent' into '(100 − x)% of the total' first — this avoids confusion about which percentage the given amount corresponds to.

question: The marked price of a bookshelf is ₹415, which is 33% above the cost price. If the profit percentage is 13%, find the discount percentage (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 15.04%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹415, which is 33% above Cost Price (CP). Profit% = 13%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CP = MP ÷ 1.33 = 415 ÷ 1.33 ≈ ₹312.03.

 

• Since profit% = 13%, Selling Price (SP) = CP × 1.13 = 312.03 × 1.13 ≈ ₹352.59.

 

• Discount = MP − SP = 415 − 352.59 = ₹62.41.

 

• Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (62.41 ÷ 415) × 100 ≈ 15.04%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A. (Note: the printed options carry a source-side formatting glitch where the leading digits before the decimal have been replaced by the option's own letter, e.g. 'A).04%' stands for '15.04%' — reproduced exactly as printed in the original paper.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Discount% = [(MP − SP)/MP] × 100. Compute CP from MP using the mark-up %, then SP from CP using the profit %, then plug directly into the discount% formula — no need for separate discount-amount tricks here since MP, mark-up% and profit% are all given.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'marked price is 33% above cost price' with 'profit is 33%' — mark-up is calculated on cost price, while discount is calculated on marked price; keep the bases straight.

question: If the surface area of a sphere increases by 69%, what is the percentage increase in its volume?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 119.7%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Surface area of a sphere increases by 69%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Surface area, S = 4πr², so S ∝ r². If S increases by 69%, new S = 1.69 × old S.

 

• Since r² ∝ S, new r² = 1.69 × old r² ⇒ new r = √1.69 × old r = 1.3 × old r (as √1.69 = 1.3).

 

• Volume, V = (4/3)πr³, so V ∝ r³. New V = (1.3)³ × old V = 2.197 × old V.

 

• Percentage increase in volume = (2.197 − 1) × 100 = 119.7%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D. (Note: the printed options show a formatting glitch where leading digits are replaced by the option's own letter, e.g. 'D).7%' stands for '119.7%' — reproduced exactly as printed.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since S ∝ r² and V ∝ r³, if S becomes k times, r becomes √k times, and V becomes k^(3/2) times. Here k = 1.69, so V-factor = 1.69^1.5 = 1.3³ = 2.197 → 119.7% increase.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever surface area/area changes are linked to volume changes for similar solids, convert everything through the linear dimension (radius/side) using the appropriate power (² for area, ³ for volume).

question: A train passes two tunnels of length 2492 m and 1914 m in 81 seconds and 64 seconds, respectively. What is the length of the train (in m)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 262 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Tunnel 1: length 2492 m, time 81 s. Tunnel 2: length 1914 m, time 64 s.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the length of the train be L m and its speed be v m/s.

 

• Crossing a tunnel means covering (tunnel length + train length): (L + 2492)/81 = v and (L + 1914)/64 = v.

 

• Equate: (L + 2492)/81 = (L + 1914)/64.

 

• Cross-multiply: 64(L + 2492) = 81(L + 1914) ⇒ 64L + 1,59,488 = 81L + 1,55,034.

 

• 1,59,488 − 1,55,034 = 81L − 64L ⇒ 4,454 = 17L ⇒ L = 4,454 ÷ 17 = 262 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the same train crosses two different fixed lengths in two different times, set (L + d₁)/t₁ = (L + d₂)/t₂ and cross-multiply directly — this single equation always solves for L without needing the speed separately.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Crossing a tunnel/platform/bridge' always means the train covers (its own length + the tunnel/platform length); 'crossing a pole/man' means it covers just its own length.

question: The sum of the modes of the data sets {1, 7, 3, 7, 3, x} and {4, 8, 9, 8, 4, y} is 11. If x > y, then find the possible correct relation between x and y.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. x − y = 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Set 1 = {1, 7, 3, 7, 3, x}: without x, 7 and 3 both already appear twice (a tie).

 

• Set 2 = {4, 8, 9, 8, 4, y}: without y, 8 and 4 both already appear twice (a tie).

 

• Sum of modes = 11, and x > y.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In Set 1, x must break the 7-3 tie to give a single mode: if x = 7, mode = 7 (appears 3 times); if x = 3, mode = 3 (appears 3 times).

 

• In Set 2, similarly: if y = 8, mode = 8; if y = 4, mode = 4.

 

• We need mode(Set 1) + mode(Set 2) = 11. Testing combinations: mode1 = 7, mode2 = 4 → 7 + 4 = 11 ✓ (this needs x = 7, y = 4).

 

• Check x > y: 7 > 4 ✓ — this is the valid combination.

 

• So x = 7, y = 4 ⇒ x − y = 7 − 4 = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a data set has a 'tied' pair of most-frequent values, the extra element x almost always must equal one of the tied values (to create a clear single mode); test both possibilities for each set and match against the given sum condition.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check the extra condition given (here x > y) at the end — it's often what picks the unique valid combination out of multiple mathematically possible ones.

question: Simplify: 35x³y²z/7xy⁴ ÷ 25xy⁻²z
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. x/5.

 

GIVEN

 

• (35x³y²z / 7xy⁴) ÷ 25xy⁻²z

 

SOLUTION

 

• First simplify 35x³y²z / 7xy⁴ = 5x^(3−1) y^(2−4) z = 5x² y⁻² z.

 

• Now divide by 25xy⁻²z, i.e. multiply by its reciprocal 1/(25xy⁻²z) = y²/(25xz): 5x²y⁻²z × y²/(25xz).

 

• Multiply numerators and denominators: (5x²y⁻²z × y²) / (25xz) = 5x²z / (25xz) [since y⁻²×y² = y⁰ = 1].

 

• = 5x²z / 25xz = 5x/25 = x/5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine all powers of each variable (x, y, z) algebraically first using exponent rules (a^m/a^n = a^(m−n)) before dividing — this avoids handling negative exponents twice.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember: dividing by a term is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, and y⁻² in a denominator becomes y² when it moves to the numerator (or vice versa).

question: Simplify: (x² + 10x + 25)/(x + 5) − 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. x.

 

GIVEN

 

• (x² + 10x + 25)/(x + 5) − 5

 

SOLUTION

 

• Factorise the numerator: x² + 10x + 25 = (x + 5)² [since it fits a² + 2ab + b² with a = x, b = 5].

 

• So (x + 5)²/(x + 5) = (x + 5), for x ≠ −5.

 

• Now subtract 5: (x + 5) − 5 = x.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Instantly recognise perfect-square trinomials of the form a² + 2ab + b² = (a+b)²; here 10x = 2 × x × 5 and 25 = 5², confirming it's (x+5)² at a glance.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check whether a quadratic numerator over a linear denominator is a perfect square before doing long division — it usually simplifies instantly.

question: A water tank is initially one-tenth full. Pipe A can empty the tank in 6 minutes. After this, pipes A, B and C are opened together to fill the tank, where pipe B can fill it in 30 minutes and pipe C in 40 minutes. How long will it take to completely fill the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 24 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Tank is initially 1/10 full. Pipe A alone empties this 1/10-full tank in 6 minutes. Pipe B fills the (full) tank in 30 minutes; Pipe C fills it in 40 minutes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take the tank's capacity as the LCM of 30 and 40 = 120 units.

 

• 'Pipe A empties the current (1/10-full) tank in 6 minutes' means A drains 1/10 of 120 = 12 units in 6 minutes, i.e. A's rate = 2 units/min. So A alone would empty a *full* tank (120 units) in 120 ÷ 2 = 60 minutes.

 

• Rate of B = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 units/min (filling). Rate of C = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/min (filling).

 

• Phase 1 (given): Pipe A alone first drains the existing 12 units down to 0 in exactly 6 minutes — the tank is now completely empty.

 

• Phase 2: Now A, B and C are opened together. Net rate = −2 (A draining) + 4 (B filling) + 3 (C filling) = +5 units/min.

 

• Time to fill the empty tank (120 units) at 5 units/min = 120 ÷ 5 = 24 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In combined pipe problems with one outlet (leak) pipe, always convert every pipe's given time into a rate on a common LCM-based capacity, and combine with correct sign (+ for fill, − for empty) before finding the time for the relevant phase.

 

NOTE

 

• Read carefully whether the 'time to empty' given refers to the full tank or to the tank's current partial level — here it describes draining just the existing 1/10, which fixes A's true full-tank rate as 60 minutes, not 6.

question:
Which number should replace the question mark (?) in the following equation?

(57.6 ÷ 4.5 × 1.5) = ? × 1/5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 96.

 

GIVEN

 

• (57.6 ÷ 4.5 × 1.5) = ? × 1/5

 

SOLUTION

 

• Left side: 57.6 ÷ 4.5 = 12.8. Then 12.8 × 1.5 = 19.2.

 

• Equation becomes: 19.2 = ? × 1/5 = ?/5.

 

• So ? = 19.2 × 5 = 96.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D. (Options A and C in the source show a formatting glitch where a leading digit is replaced by the option's own letter — reproduced exactly as printed.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• '? × 1/5' is the same as '?/5', so simply multiply the computed left-hand value by 5 to isolate '?' — avoids dealing with fractions awkwardly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify the known (numeric) side of the equation completely first (BODMAS: ÷ and × left to right), then isolate the unknown in one final step.

question: A company sells an article at a price such that it earns a 25% profit on the selling price. What is the actual profit percentage on the cost price? (correct to two decimal places)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 33.33%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Profit = 25% of Selling Price (SP), not of Cost Price (CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let SP = ₹100. Profit = 25% of SP = ₹25.

 

• Cost Price = SP − Profit = 100 − 25 = ₹75.

 

• Profit% on cost price = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (25 ÷ 75) × 100 = 33.33%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A. (All four printed options show the same source-side formatting glitch — a leading digit replaced by the option's own letter, so each displays as 'X).33%'; only Option A is marked correct in the original answer key.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If profit is given as p% of SP, then profit% on CP = [p / (100 − p)] × 100. Here p = 25, so profit% on CP = (25/75) × 100 = 33.33% — instant formula, no need to assume SP = 100 each time.

 

NOTE

 

• Never confuse 'profit on selling price' with 'profit on cost price' — profit percentage is conventionally calculated on cost price unless the question explicitly states otherwise, as it does here.

question: If 30% of 50% of 2/3 of a number is 325, find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3250.

 

GIVEN

 

• 30% of 50% of (2/3) of a number = 325.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert all to fractions/decimals and multiply: 0.30 × 0.50 × (2/3) = 0.30 × 0.50 × 0.6667 = 0.10.

 

• So 10% of the number = 325.

 

• Number = 325 ÷ 0.10 = 3250.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Multiply the successive fractions first: 30% × 50% = 15%; 15% × (2/3) = 10%. So the number = 325 ÷ 10% = 325 × 10 = 3250.

 

NOTE

 

• Combine all the successive percentage/fraction operations into a single overall fraction of the number before dividing — much faster than working step by step.

question: If the height of a cylinder is 15 cm and its base area is 169π cm², then find its total surface area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2288 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Height (h) of cylinder = 15 cm. Base area = πr² = 169π cm².

 

SOLUTION

 

• From base area: πr² = 169π ⇒ r² = 169 ⇒ r = 13 cm.

 

• Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = 2πr(h + r).

 

• TSA = 2π × 13 × (15 + 13) = 2π × 13 × 28 = 728π cm².

 

• Using π ≈ 22/7: TSA = 728 × 22/7 = 104 × 22 = 2288 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always find r first from the given base area (πr²), then plug directly into TSA = 2πr(h+r); using π = 22/7 keeps the arithmetic in clean integers when r is a multiple of 7's factors.

 

NOTE

 

• Total Surface Area of a cylinder = 2πrh (curved surface) + 2πr² (two circular ends) = 2πr(h + r); don't confuse it with Curved Surface Area alone (2πrh).

question:
What will come in place of 'A' in the following ratio?

180/A = 11/44
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 720.

 

GIVEN

 

• 180/A = 11/44

 

SOLUTION

 

• Cross-multiply: 180 × 44 = 11 × A.

 

• 180 × 44 = 7,920.

 

• A = 7,920 ÷ 11 = 720.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify 11/44 = 1/4 first. Then 180/A = 1/4 ⇒ A = 180 × 4 = 720 — much faster than cross-multiplying the unsimplified fraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check if the given fraction can be reduced to lowest terms before cross-multiplying — it often turns messy arithmetic into a one-step mental calculation.

question: If the listed price of a bag is 76% more than its cost price and a discount of 54% is announced on it, then find the loss percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 19.04%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Listed (marked) price = Cost price + 76% of cost price. Discount offered = 54% on listed price.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let CP = ₹100. Then Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 76% of 100 = ₹176.

 

• Discount = 54% of MP = 0.54 × 176 = ₹95.04.

 

• Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 176 − 95.04 = ₹80.96.

 

• Since SP (₹80.96) < CP (₹100), there is a loss. Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 80.96 = ₹19.04.

 

• Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (19.04 ÷ 100) × 100 = 19.04%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A. (The printed options carry a source-side formatting glitch where the leading digits are replaced by the option's own letter, e.g. 'A).04%' stands for '19.04%' — reproduced exactly as printed in the original paper.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net % change when price is marked up by a% and then discounted by b% = a − b − (ab/100). Here a = 76, b = 54: Net = 76 − 54 − (76×54/100) = 22 − 41.04 = −19.04%, i.e. a loss of 19.04% — a one-line shortcut avoiding the CP/MP/SP chain above.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute mark-up on CP and discount on MP (marked price) — using the wrong base is the most common error in profit-loss-discount chains like this one.

question: A ladder is leaning against a wall. The foot of the ladder is 1115.4705 cm away from the wall, and the ladder makes an angle of 60 degrees with the ground. Find the height of the wall it touches. (Round your answer to the nearest integer.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1932 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Base (foot of ladder to wall) = 1115.4705 cm. Angle with the ground = 60°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In the right triangle formed by the wall, ground, and ladder: tan(angle) = height/base (Height = opposite side to the angle, Base = adjacent side).

 

• Height = base × tan60° = 1115.4705 × √3 = 1115.4705 × 1.7320508.

 

• Height ≈ 1932.0 cm, which rounds to 1932 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a 60° angle with the ground, Height = Base × √3 (√3 ≈ 1.732); for a 30° angle, Height = Base/√3 — memorise these two standard multipliers to solve ladder/angle-of-elevation questions instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• tan60° = √3 ≈ 1.732; tan45° = 1; tan30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577 — these standard trigonometric ratios are essential and frequently tested in RRB exams.

question: The amount on a sum of ₹6,800 at the rate of 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹8,228.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal (P) = ₹6,800. Rate (R) = 10% per annum, compounded annually. Time (T) = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Amount = P × (1 + R/100)^T = 6,800 × (1.1)².

 

• (1.1)² = 1.21.

 

• Amount = 6,800 × 1.21 = ₹8,228.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 2 years at rate R%, the compound multiplying factor is (1 + R/100)² = 1 + 2(R/100) + (R/100)² — at R=10%, this is 1 + 0.20 + 0.01 = 1.21, so Amount = P × 1.21 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• For CI over 2 years at rate R%, effective rate = [2R + R²/100]%; here effective rate = 20 + 1 = 21%, so Amount = 6800 × 1.21 = 8228 — same result via the effective-rate shortcut.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 25% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 83% and that of the TV decreases by 15%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 8 washing machines and 4 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Increase by 43.8%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost = 25% less than TV cost. WM cost increases by 83%; TV cost decreases by 15%. Find % change in total cost of 8 WMs + 4 TVs.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = ₹100. Then WM cost = 100 − 25% of 100 = ₹75.

 

• Old total cost = 8 × 75 + 4 × 100 = 600 + 400 = ₹1000.

 

• New WM cost = 75 × 1.83 = ₹137.25. New TV cost = 100 × 0.85 = ₹85.

 

• New total cost = 8 × 137.25 + 4 × 85 = 1098 + 340 = ₹1438.

 

• % change = [(1438 − 1000)/1000] × 100 = 43.8% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A. (The printed option shows a formatting glitch where the leading digits are replaced by the option's letter, i.e. 'A).8%' stands for '43.8%' — reproduced exactly as printed.)

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume a convenient base value (TV = 100) to instantly get WM = 75 from the 25%-less condition, then compute old and new weighted totals directly — avoids working with unknowns/variables.

 

NOTE

 

• '25% less than TV' means WM = 75% of TV cost, not TV = 75% of WM cost — always identify which quantity is the reference (100%) base carefully.

question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 5 days. B alone can do the same work in 10 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• (A + B) together finish 1 work in 5 days. B alone finishes 1 work in 10 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rate of (A + B) = 1/5 work/day. Rate of B = 1/10 work/day.

 

• Rate of A = Rate of (A+B) − Rate of B = 1/5 − 1/10 = 2/10 − 1/10 = 1/10 work/day.

 

• So A alone takes 10 days to complete 1 work.

 

• To do double the work (2 units of work), A alone takes 2 × 10 = 20 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Work and time are directly proportional for the same worker: if 1 work takes T days, 2× work takes 2T days — no need to recompute rates for 'double work' once the single-work time is known.

 

NOTE

 

• Subtracting rates (not times) is the correct way to find an individual's rate from a combined rate and a partner's rate — never subtract the number of days directly.

question: Prakhar and Riya together invested ₹56,700 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹5,400, Prakhar's share was ₹1,400. What was Prakhar's investment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹14,700.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹56,700. Total profit = ₹5,400, of which Prakhar's share = ₹1,400.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Riya's profit share = Total profit − Prakhar's share = 5,400 − 1,400 = ₹4,000.

 

• Profit ratio, Prakhar : Riya = 1,400 : 4,000 = 7 : 20 (dividing both by 200).

 

• Since profit share ∝ investment (assuming equal time period), investment ratio is also 7 : 20, total parts = 27.

 

• Prakhar's investment = (7/27) × 56,700 = 7 × 2,100 = ₹14,700.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In a simple partnership (same time period for both partners), profit ratio = investment ratio directly — convert the given profit split into its simplest ratio, then apply that same ratio to the total investment.

 

NOTE

 

• 56,700 ÷ 27 = 2,100 divides evenly, a good check that the simplified ratio (7:20, sum 27) was computed correctly.

question: The price of 3 pens is equal to the price of 5 pencils. The price of 5 pens and 3 pencils is ₹34. The price of 3 pen and 5 pencils is ₹____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹30.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 × (price of pen) = 5 × (price of pencil). Also, 5 pens + 3 pencils = ₹34.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let price of 1 pen = P, price of 1 pencil = C. Given: 3P = 5C ⇒ P = 5C/3.

 

• Given: 5P + 3C = 34. Substitute P: 5 × (5C/3) + 3C = 34 ⇒ 25C/3 + 3C = 34 ⇒ (25C + 9C)/3 = 34 ⇒ 34C/3 = 34 ⇒ C = 3.

 

• So P = 5 × 3/3 = 5.

 

• Price of 3 pens + 5 pencils = 3P + 5C = 3(5) + 5(3) = 15 + 15 = ₹30.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice the symmetry: since 3P = 5C, swapping the coefficients of P and C in '5P+3C' to get '3P+5C' is a classic exam trick — solve for individual values once, then just plug into the second expression.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert 'price of X items = price of Y items' into a simple ratio/equation between unit prices first — it's the key that unlocks the rest of the problem.

question:
Bhanu travels from City A to City B. If Bhanu drives his car at 1/3rd of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 50 minutes late.

 

Find the time (in minutes) that Bhanu would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 25.

 

GIVEN

 

• Reduced speed = (1/3) × normal speed. This causes a delay of 50 minutes compared to the normal-speed journey.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since distance is constant, time is inversely proportional to speed. If speed becomes 1/3, time becomes 3 times the normal time.

 

• Let normal time = T minutes. New time = 3T minutes.

 

• Extra (delay) time = 3T − T = 2T = 50 minutes.

 

• T = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If speed becomes 1/n of normal, time becomes n times normal, so extra time = (n−1) × T. Here n = 3, extra time = 2T = 50 ⇒ T = 25 — a one-line shortcut for all such 'speed reduced to a fraction, reaches late' problems.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed and time are inversely proportional for a fixed distance — this relationship, S₁T₁ = S₂T₂, is the foundation of virtually all such problems.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

835 836 839 844 851 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 860.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 835, 836, 839, 844, 851, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 836−835=1, 839−836=3, 844−839=5, 851−844=7.

 

• The differences form the pattern of consecutive odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, ..., so the next difference is 9.

 

• Next term = 851 + 9 = 860.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a series' consecutive differences grow slowly and steadily, immediately check if they follow the odd-number sequence (1,3,5,7,9,...) or even-number sequence — a very common RRB series pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute at least 3-4 consecutive differences before concluding the pattern — a single difference can be misleading.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

Some dolls are pencils.

Some fingers are pencils.

 

Conclusions:

(I): All fingers are dolls.

(II): Some dolls are fingers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: Some dolls are pencils (I-type). Statement 2: Some fingers are pencils (I-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Both premises are particular affirmative (I-type) statements, sharing the common (middle) term 'pencils'.

 

• By the standard rules of syllogism, two 'Some...are' (I-type) premises never yield any valid conclusion — there is no guaranteed overlap between 'dolls' and 'fingers' just because both overlap with 'pencils' separately (they could overlap in entirely different pencils, or not connect to each other at all).

 

• Drawing this on a Venn diagram: dolls and pencils overlap somewhere, fingers and pencils overlap somewhere else — but nothing forces dolls and fingers to overlap. So both conclusions are not guaranteed.

 

• Conclusion I ('All fingers are dolls') is a universal claim, far too strong to follow from two 'Some' statements. Conclusion II ('Some dolls are fingers') is also not guaranteed since the two 'some pencils' groups need not be the same pencils.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rule of thumb: I + I premises → No valid conclusion (in standard syllogism, particular + particular premises never validly combine). Spotting this pattern instantly rules out both given conclusions here.

 

NOTE

 

• Always draw quick Venn diagrams for syllogism questions when in doubt — try to draw a valid scenario where the conclusion is FALSE; if you can, the conclusion does not follow.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

105 87 69 51 33 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 105, 87, 69, 51, 33, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences: 87−105=−18, 69−87=−18, 51−69=−18, 33−51=−18.

 

• The series decreases by a constant 18 each time (an arithmetic progression).

 

• Next term = 33 − 18 = 15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When the differences between consecutive terms are all identical, it's a simple arithmetic progression — just subtract (or add) that common difference once more to get the next term.

 

NOTE

 

• Constant-difference series are the simplest and fastest to spot; always check for a constant difference before looking for more complex patterns.

question: EHLQ is related to GKNT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, MTTC is related to OWVF. To which of the given options is SCZL related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. UFBO.

 

GIVEN

 

• EHLQ → GKNT and MTTC → OWVF follow the same coding logic; find the equivalent for SCZL.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to positions (A=1...Z=26) and find the shift for each letter of EHLQ→GKNT: E(5)→G(7): +2; H(8)→K(11): +3; L(12)→N(14): +2; Q(17)→T(20): +3.

 

• Pattern of shifts: +2, +3, +2, +3 (alternating). Verify with MTTC→OWVF: M(13)→O(15): +2; T(20)→W(23): +3; T(20)→V(22): +2; C(3)→F(6): +3. Same +2,+3,+2,+3 pattern confirmed. ✓
